question: Identify the precipitate formed when carbon dioxide gas is passed through lime water.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcium carbonate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Calcium carbonate:**

 
 
• When carbon dioxide (CO₂) gas is passed through lime water (calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂), a white precipitate of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) is formed.
 
• This reaction is a classic chemical test for the presence of carbon dioxide.
 
• The chemical equation for the reaction is: Ca(OH)₂ (aq) + CO₂ (g) → CaCO₃ (s) + H₂O (l).<
